root_motivation: The registry in src/handler.rs mixes host.<family>_<verb> (host.tool_publish, host.tool_share, host.key_rotate, ...) with host.<family>.<verb> (host.docs.put, host.agent.lookup, host.group.create, ...) and two un-prefixed families (signup, billing.*), with no rule written down anywhere. Synthorg's scripted explorer already invented dotted variants that don't exist (host.tool.call_shared, host.tool.recall) and a chain's ledger probe calls a nonexistent host.calls.list -- integrators guess, and guess wrong, costing a tool_not_found and a lost minute every time.
user_persona: An agent operator integrating mcphost for the first time, whose client autocompletes a new host.* call from a sibling family's name; an existing client whose code already calls an old underscored name; an operator deciding when an alias's usage has dropped enough to sunset it.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the registry at the landing commit, When scripts/tool-naming-lint.sh runs, Then it exits 0, lists each documented exception with its reason, and reports violations=0 aliases=<n>; given a fixture registering host.secret_delete, Then it exits 1 naming host.secret.delete.

Given a client calling host.tool_share with valid arguments, When dispatched, Then the result equals a call to host.tool.share with the same arguments, the response carries the deprecation hint (where the protocol allows), and exactly one tool_deprecated_alias log line appears for that tenant that day across 5 calls.

Given tools/list, When fetched, Then every canonical name is present, every alias is present with x-deprecated.replaced_by equal to its canonical and a sunset date 90 days after landing, and the alias's inputSchema equals the canonical's.

Given docs/** and plugin/** at the landing commit, When the docs-names test runs, Then every host.*/billing.*/signup literal exists in the registry, and docs/tools.md is byte-identical to a fresh gen-docs run.
Given the alias metrics, When 3 alias calls and 2 canonical calls happen for a tool with a deprecated alias, Then the counter named in docs/metrics.md reads alias=3 canonical=2.
Given an unknown name one edit away from a canonical (host.tool.shar), When called, Then tool_not_found includes did_you_mean: ["host.tool.share"].
Given a new session's first host.whoami, When answered, Then the response includes naming_rule_url; the second call in the session does not.
Given the existing test suite, When any test asserted an exact tools/list count, Then it is updated to the new count with a comment citing this PRD, and no other test changed.
Given cargo test at the landing commit, When it runs, Then every previously passing test passes and the toolname_* tests for AC 1-8 pass.

additional.test_file_names_use_test_prefix_toolname: test_prefix toolname (the PRD's own frontmatter field): tests/toolname_ac<NN>_<slug>.rs, same convention as every other test file in this repo.

five_whys_trace.q: Why keep every old underscored name working as an alias instead of just renaming in place?
five_whys_trace.a: Goal 2 is explicit ("zero breaking changes"), and the grounding incident is guesswork from a client reading one name and guessing another's shape -- breaking the two paying-path clients that already exist would trade one integration-friction problem for a worse one.

five_whys_trace.q: Why inject the alias as a cloned Tool entry in host_tools() rather than a second hand-written Tool::new call per alias?
five_whys_trace.a: A hand-written twin would drift the moment the canonical's schema/description changed; cloning guarantees AC3's own 'alias's inputSchema equals the canonical's' by construction instead of by discipline.

five_whys_trace.q: Why resolve an alias to its canonical before dispatch_tenant_tool's match, rather than adding a second match arm per alias?
five_whys_trace.a: dispatch_tenant_tool's ~150-arm match already names each canonical exactly once; duplicating arms for 20 aliases would double the places a future edit to one handler's call site has to touch. Resolving once in call_tool keeps the match the single source of canonical-name-to-handler wiring.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is the per-tenant-per-day log dedup and the alias-call metric an in-memory, process-wide static instead of a DB table?
five_whys_trace.a: Same tradeoff this crate's own help_url_served{code} counter already makes (help.rs's own doc comment) -- host-wide telemetry for an operator's sunset decision, not a durable per-call audit record; a DB migration for it would be new surface this PRD's requirements don't ask for.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does AppError::host_tool_not_found's did_you_mean search only canonical names, never a registered alias, even when an alias is the closer edit-distance match?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 6's own point is steering a typo toward the name this PRD wants integrators to learn; suggesting another deprecated name would just relocate the guesswork this PRD exists to remove.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Dotted canonical (default) vs underscore canonical?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Dotted, per the PRD's own open-question resolution ("coder proceeds with dotted unless told") and the registry's own already-dominant style (host.docs.put, host.agent.lookup, host.group.create, ...).

ambiguities_resolved.question: Sunset length?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: 90 days from this PRD's own landing work (2026-10-02), per the PRD's own open-question resolution ("90 days default") -- SUNSET_DATE = 2026-12-31, a fixed commitment rather than a rolling landing-date computation, so tools/list's x-deprecated.sunset doesn't change on every call.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the MCP _meta field survive every client SDK? If not, where does the deprecation hint go?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: _meta.deprecated is always attached to a successful alias call's CallToolResult regardless of client support -- a client that drops _meta simply never sees it, same as any other _meta extension; tools/list's x-deprecated and the tool_deprecated_alias log line are the two channels guaranteed to survive any client.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which singleton-noun host.<noun> tools (no sibling verb) get a lint exception beyond the PRD's own 5 named examples (host.whoami, host.redeem, host.quickstart, host.changelog, host.usage)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: host.export and host.progress, found by applying the PRD's own stated rule ("no sibling verbs route under this family") systematically across the full registry rather than treating the 5 named examples as the exhaustive list.
